solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: to master a difficulty is to get the better of it, defeat it
someone speechless with emotion is overwhelmed by feeling

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings: to get the better of something, and so moved that you cannot speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a verb meaning conquer, and an adjective meaning overwhelmed by emotion.

clue.text: Piece in good books about divine chaps

indicators.note: about means the books go round the other letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the good books
DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a divine
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A passage in the Bible concerning holy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun here: a clergyman, abbreviated DD for Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap or remnant is a stray piece of something.

indicators.note: in places the article inside the Gaelic word

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Irish Gaelic
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove an article written in Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to wipe out or remove written material.

clue.text: All cables are deciphered and readily understood

indicators.note: deciphered means the scrambled letters are worked out into plain text

explanation.surface: Coded telegrams have all been decoded and their meaning is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly clear and easy to understand, like a bell's ring.

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
agog means eagerly curious

explanation.surface: A young woman fascinated by a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, famous as figures guarding London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend and in the Bible Magog is named alongside Gog, and the pair are pictured as giants.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: returning means the word for the payment is read backwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: A grievance from a bishop about money being paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a grumble or grievance, as in 'What's your problem with him?'

indicators.note: in places the inner letters inside the jug

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug, a vessel
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Letting a Member of Parliament cross over in a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a jug, a ewer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the power or authority to do something is to allow them.

indicators.note: leaves means the knight's letter departs from the clothing word

parts.note: finery is elaborate, showy dress
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: An ardent knight walks out of a display of fancy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe intense, burning emotion or temper.

clue.text: Philosopher showing sense isn't upset with Genet

parts.note: wit is good sense, as in 'have the wit to'

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker shows that sense is upset by the writer Genet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Genet was a French writer. 'with' joins the two words that are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig Wittgenstein was an Austrian-British philosopher of logic and language.

parts.note: a rake is a man of loose, immoral habits

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I's court favourite described as a duke and a libertine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake, the sea captain who sailed round the world, was a favourite of Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis, the Elizabethan navigator and privateer, enjoyed the Queen's high favour.

parts.note: a view lasting only a short time is a brief, passing look

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-term view' sounds like a policy outlook, but read literally it is a look that lasts only a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleeting, momentary look at something is literally a view of short duration.

definitions.meaning: the organ of sight is the part of you that does the looking
to catch someone's attention is to catch their gaze

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings: the organ that looks, and notice or attention, as in 'catch someone's eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of sight looks; and the word also means watchful notice, as in 'under the eye of'.

parts.note: the Tories are the political right
someone out is not at home, away

explanation.surface: A protester's slogan demanding the Conservatives leave office immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without any delay at all.

clue.text: Saw middle of fire must spread

indicators.note: spread means the gathered letters are scattered and laid out afresh
middle of takes the central letters of the word fire

explanation.surface: A warning that the heart of a blaze will inevitably spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not a tool or a past tense: it is an old saying. 'spread' shuffles IR (the middle of FIRE) with MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and a self-evident statement is a similar commonplace.

indicators.note: centre picks the two central letters of the word refugees

parts.note: and means with, in addition to

explanation.surface: An African among the refugees at a centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Uganda, a country in East Africa, is an African.

clue.text: Flutter involving one sport generates capital

indicators.note: involving means the bet wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet
I is the Roman numeral for one
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A gamble on a sport paying off as a large sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money won, but it is a capital city: Lebanon's. A flutter is British slang for a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.

clue.text: That place accommodating a tragedy, initially?

definitions.text: That place accommodating a tragedy, initially?

indicators.note: accommodating means the place word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of tragedy

explanation.surface: A venue that stages a tragedy, described from its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is the venue where a tragedy is staged, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Stale lamb minced for seasoned dish

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up small, so the letters are cut up and reformed

explanation.surface: Old lamb put through the mincer to make a spiced dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls of spiced minced meat make a seasoned dish, served with pasta or in sauce.

clue.text: Tightwad — or man giving tons away?

indicators.note: giving with away means handing over and losing the letter
away completes the phrase giving away, so the letter goes

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: Is a skinflint a man who donates tons of money?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's generous man is the opposite of the answer, a joke at the miser's expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightwad is slang for a mean person who hoards money and hates spending it.

definitions.meaning: an ox is a beast that lows, or moos
to look dark and threatening, also spelt lour, as clouds or a frowning face do

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings: a creature that moos, and to frown or look threatening, pronounced to rhyme with 'flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, so an ox is a mooing animal; and the verb means to scowl or darken threateningly.

indicators.note: shortened means the word for the contest loses its last letter

parts.note: a duel is a contest between two people

explanation.surface: A fair fight that was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper or appropriate, as in 'with due respect' or 'in due course'.

clue.text: Bend up to hug English star

indicators.note: to hug means the reversed word wraps round the letter
in a down clue up means the word bend is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Instructions to bend upwards and embrace an English celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus.

clue.text: Saint Oswald somehow creates facetious precept

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters are rearranged in some way or other

explanation.surface: A saint's name is turned into a jokey rule of life.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British name for the jocular rule that if something can go wrong, it will, also called Murphy's law.
explanation.definitionFit: The jokey principle that whatever can go wrong will go wrong is a mock-serious rule.

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the phrase modern style

explanation.surface: A surrealist artist working in a modern manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter of the Dada and Surrealist movements.

clue.text: Mysterious character takes ecstasy after work

indicators.note: after places the drug letter following the word for work

parts.note: a machine that runs is working
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure takes drugs after a day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, not a person: an ancient letter carved in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, often given magical or secret meaning.

clue.text: Be longer wandering in French city

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to linger while strolling around a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps, in the south-east of France.
